name: Hamul
overview: Hamul was a male member of the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the son of Perez and the grandson of Judah. He is listed among the sons of Israel who journeyed to Egypt, marking him as part of the foundational generations of the Israelite people. His descendants, known as the Hamulites, are mentioned in the census records of the wilderness period.
namesAndTitles: The name Hamul means "pitied," reflecting a proper name given in the Hebrew context. There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, but it carries a meaningful Hebrew significance as recorded in Genesis 46:12.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Hamul as the son of Perez, who was himself a son of Judah. This establishes Hamul within the direct lineage of the tribe of Judah, linking him to the patriarchal family of Israel.
scriptureSignificance: Hamul's significance lies in his place within the genealogical record of Israel, particularly as a descendant of Judah through Perez. His inclusion among those who went to Egypt situates him in the larger narrative of Israel's formation and migration, which sets the stage for God's unfolding plan of redemption. The mention of the Hamulites in the wilderness census further emphasizes the ongoing legacy of his lineage within the nation of Israel.
